title: Answer to Question: The Judges' Crisis in Pakistan, Its Escalation and the Way It Was Resolved, and the Focus on Nawaz Sharif
text:
Answer to Question: The judges' crisis in Pakistan, its escalation and the way it was resolved, and the focus on Nawaz Sharif

Question:

In the past week matters came to a crisis in Pakistan between the government and Nawaz Sharif. He was placed under house arrest on 15/3/2009 CE, then he defied the house arrest... Then the US Secretary of State contacted Nawaz Sharif and Zardari... Then the crisis ended, and the government decided on 16/3/2009 CE to reinstate the judges, and Nawaz Sharif calmed down... So why did it escalate and explode, and then calm down with an American phone call?! And why, during this crisis, was the focus of America, the government of Pakistan and the media... on Nawaz Sharif and not on the other opposition leaders?

Answer:

1- As is well known, Musharraf had allowed Bhutto to come from London to Pakistan in return for a deal between America and Britain, and then between Musharraf and Bhutto. But Bhutto exploited Musharraf's crimes and the people's hatred of him, so she tried to exploit the situation in her own favour and not to abide by the deal... Later she was assassinated...

2- After that, the party leaderships in the People's Party which had gone along with the English during the period of Bhutto's exile there became alarmed, especially after the front rank of those counted as belonging to the People's Party, Zardari and Gilani, went along in America's train. If we add to that Kayani, the army chief whom America had brought in before, then America has taken hold of the threads of rule in Pakistan.

3- Thus nothing remained for Britain except the opposition, and the exploitation of America's provocations of the Pakistani people through its aircraft's continuous bombing of Pakistani territory and the killing of children and women... as well as the worsening of the economic crisis. Britain exploited these events, moved leaders in the opposition and heated up the atmosphere. At the beginning America did not see a problem in these events; rather its men were taking part with the opposition in that, because it saw an interest for itself in keeping the people occupied internally, so that it could carry out its criminal acts in the tribal region without an uproar.

However, matters worsened recently, and the men of the English almost took over the arena in the name of the opposition, in order to bring down the government or at least "disturb its peace"...

4- Then America saw that Britain was close to succeeding in moving the opposition and bringing it, if not to power, then at least to imposing its conditions on the rulers. So America's decision was that it would itself take hold of the opposition just as it had taken hold of the government.

From here came the strong moving of Nawaz Sharif in the face of the government... so that he would stand out in the opposition, and the opposition would be in its hand just as the government is in its hand, and it would cut off the path to the influence of any opposition that Britain arranges.

America controls the presidency of the state, the premiership and the chief of staff of the army. And it wants to control the opposition. That is why it made its agent Nawaz Sharif, whom it had removed from the premiership in 1999 and then returned to Pakistan from his exile a second time in 2007, it made him lead the Pakistani opposition, so that everything in Pakistan would be in its hand. This enables it, according to its plan, to prevent any true and sincere change from happening, because it holds both the government and the opposition. At the same time it obstructs the work of Britain, which is striving to return to playing an influential role in Pakistan, especially as America has not been able to liquidate it from there, and it is not easy for it to liquidate it completely, because of the existence of agents of Britain who are still embedded in some corners of the regime and in some corners of the People's Party.

5- Thus Nawaz Sharif was brought forward as leader of the opposition, and that was done in the following way:

a- On 26/2/2009 the Pakistani Supreme Court issued a decision barring Nawaz Sharif, and likewise his brother Shahbaz, from occupying any government post through elections. Following that, demonstrations organised by Nawaz Sharif's party broke out against the court's decision. One day before this date, on 25/2/2009 CE, demonstrations and marches broke out in dozens of Pakistani cities in protest at the economic situation in the country, alongside the protests against the American attacks on the country. The federal government had dismissed Shahbaz Sharif from the post of chief minister in the government of Punjab after it suspended the work of its provincial parliament and tied the province of Punjab directly to its own authority.

b- It is understood from Nawaz Sharif's movement that America wants to absorb the opposition against its agents ruling in Pakistan and to make the leadership of the opposition in its hand. By that it misleads the people and keeps them away from working in the right direction towards changing the regime in Pakistan, and it strikes those resisting it in the tribal region while keeping the people occupied with protests over a side matter, namely the return of the judges to their posts, and keeps them away from the real goal. It is as if the issue of Pakistan were the return of the judges to their posts, and that if they were returned to their posts justice would be achieved and all the country's problems would be solved. This is while the root of the discontent and of the protests is the submissiveness of the regime in Pakistan to the Americans, who are fighting those resisting American policy and demanding a return to the rule of Islam, and fighting them through their brothers in the Pakistani army, which fights alongside America; and also because of the injustice that falls upon them as a result of the implementation of a non-Islamic system.

c- Thus was Nawaz Sharif's defiance of the government's decisions and his going out against them without fear, on the basis that America had not given the government the green light to arrest him; had it been permitted to arrest him it would have done so, for what he did is sufficient justification for arresting him. The Pakistani Interior Minister Rehman Malik said at a press conference, accusing Nawaz Sharif of inciting the people to disobedience: "Inciting the people to disobedience is stirring up sedition (fitnah), and its punishment is life imprisonment." And he said: "The government does not intend to arrest him, but it has sufficient justifications for arresting him, especially in the event of violence breaking out during the marches..." (BBC, 10/3/2009)!

d- Since the events exploded, America has been following closely what is happening and going on, and indeed drawing its lines. The US State Department confirmed on 13/3/2009 that American officials were in contact with Pakistani leaders to get out of the state of political tension (Al Jazeera, 14/3/2009). This indicates that America is monitoring the crisis and working to supervise it directly.

On the America.gov website, quoting a spokesman of the US State Department: "The decision to reinstate the Chief Justice of the Pakistani Supreme Court to his post, which the Pakistani Prime Minister Gilani announced on 16/3/2009 CE, came after telephone calls that the US Secretary of State Hillary Rodham Clinton made with Pakistani leaders during the weekend of 14-15 March of this month.

The acting official spokesman of the US State Department, Robert Wood, confirmed at a press conference he held on 16 March of this month that "the Secretary of State wanted to make sure that the Pakistani officials had understood our point of view on the current situation and the importance of no violence breaking out, and the necessity of conducting a political dialogue."

e- By that America has succeeded in taking hold of the opposition, at least in the foreseeable term. We say in the foreseeable term because Britain has its men, as we said, in some corners of the People's Party, and likewise in other opposition political circles, and even some penetrations inside the government institutions themselves, even if not to an influential degree.

Accordingly, Nawaz Sharif's movement does not go beyond America's plans to create an opposition loyal to it, and for this reason the focus was put on Nawaz Sharif, rather than the rest of the opposition, in order to bring him forward as its leader.

f- America has succeeded in its calculations towards Britain, so it has taken hold of the government and the opposition. But the point of error in America's calculations is that it forgot, or pretended to forget, that the Ummah in Pakistan is in one valley and the figures of the government and the opposition are in another valley, and that what America has succeeded in is taking hold of those figures, and they are below zero in the reckoning of the Ummah, which, when it roars, will not be stood against, neither by those figures nor by their masters, whether those masters are America or Britain. "And Allah is predominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know."
